Omega Valley · art direction

Which look should Omega Valley have?

Omega Valley is a point-and-click adventure about Joseph and a village on Omega Island. We are choosing its art style. Walk Joseph around the village street in both looks, then pick the one you prefer.

Try both looks

Click the street to walk. Keys 1 and 2 switch.

Vote

Which look do you prefer? Tell Nadeem your choice and why.

Option 1: 32-bit pixel art

640 × 360 pixel grid · rooms 64 colours · characters 32 colours

What you get

  • The classic point-and-click look of games like Kathy Rain, Unavowed and Blasphemous.
  • One clean style for every room and every character.
  • Small files, and walk, talk and pick-up animations are quick to draw.

What it costs

  • All 61 rooms and 10 characters must be redrawn.
  • The realistic movie clips will not match a pixel game.
  • This sample has only a side walk; front and back walks still need drawing.

Option 2: painted rooms + 3D characters

1920 × 1080 painted rooms · 8 walk directions from one 3D model

What you get

  • Keeps the game's current painted rooms.
  • Every direction and move (walk, run, talk, pick up) comes from one model, always at the right size.
  • Closest to the look of the movie.

What it costs

  • Each character needs a real 3D model first. The Joseph here is a simple stand-in built from basic shapes.
  • The most setup work at the start.
